Proof 1: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Statement: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #1):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

ID: dab217129bfb | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'algebraically closed': rotation in R^2 has no real eigenvalue

Provenance: Variation #1 for theorem in domain Linear Algebra

Proof 2: Spectral theorem: self-adjoint operator has orthonormal eigenbasis

Statement: Spectral theorem: self-adjoint operator has orthonormal eigenbasis

Hypotheses: H finite-dim Hilbert space, T self-adjoint

Conclusion: orthonormal basis of eigenvectors

Definitions: self-adjoint, eigenvalue, orthonormal

Proof (Variation #2):

Step 1: Eigenvalues of self-adjoint are real

Step 2: Eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal

Step 3: Sum of dimensions equals dim(H)

Step 4: Restrict T to orthogonal complement

Step 5: Apply induction on dimension

ID: e35cd3614211 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'self-adjoint': non-normal matrices may not be diagonalizable

Provenance: Variation #2 for theorem in domain Linear Algebra

Proof 217: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Statement: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #217):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Statement: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #539):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Proof 683: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Statement: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #683):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #789):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Mutation test: Removing 'algebraically closed': rotation in R^2 has no real eigenvalue

Proof 897: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Statement: Every linear transformation T: V -> V has eigenvalue (over alg. closed field)

Hypotheses: V finite-dimensional, F algebraically closed, T: V -> V linear

Conclusion: T has at least one eigenvalue

Definitions: eigenvalue, characteristic polynomial, algebraically closed

Proof (Variation #897):

Step 1: Choose basis, represent T as matrix A

Step 2: Compute characteristic polynomial p(t) = det(A - tI)

Step 3: p(t) has degree n = dim(V) > 0

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Step 4: F algebraically closed => p has root lambda

Step 5: A v = lambda v for nonzero v, so lambda is eigenvalue

Extra proofs (2 theorems from expanded bank)

Proof 1: Ext^n_R(M,N) classifies extensions of M by N

Statement: Ext^n_R(M,N) classifies extensions of M by N

Hypotheses: M left R-module, N right R-module

Conclusion: Ext^1 classifies short exact sequences 0->N->E->M->0

Definitions: Ext, extension, derived functor

Proof:

Step 1: Take projective resolution of M

Step 2: Apply Hom(-,N)
